notes: Independently assessed all 14 discovery/diamond candidates and read the fee audit. This file changes difficulty and metrics only; no fee route, eligibility, format or scope field is replaced.

Six high bands are explicitly agent judgments about demanding contribution criteria within the relevant health-systems specialty: Medical Care Research and Review; Health Services Management Research; Journal of Health Organization and Management; Health Care Management Science; Journal of Medical Systems; International Journal of Medical Informatics. Eight remain unknown. Unknown does not mean easy, less rigorous or low quality; these bands do not estimate manuscript-specific acceptance probabilities or rank unrelated disciplines.

Nine dated, completed-year citation metrics were verified on current official Emerald/Springer journal pages for four journals. WHO's explicit 2025 impact-factor label is documented in its audit note, but excluded from metrics because the underlying JCR period could not be independently established. Raw citation/document counts were not published on the inspected pages; no counts were invented.

Standard JIF windows are interpreted using the official publisher definition at https://www.sagepub.com/journals/understanding-journal-metrics (JCR-year citations, preceding two or five publication years). CiteScore's four-year eligible-document framework is described on the official Emerald journal page https://www.emeraldgrouppublishing.com/journal/jhom?id=jhom; the eligible types/window were verified in its indexed official text. Definitions are distinct from venue-specific numerical evidence. Citation impact is never used alone to set difficulty.

The current migrated Emerald homepages show acceptance percentages without a cohort period, whereas older official journal/finder pages indexed in search show different values associated with earlier material. No acceptance statistic was retained or used for a band because an exact current period/population could not be established. The old pages' values were not assigned to the new page's cohort.

Sage author instructions were readable, but journal metrics/overview endpoints were inaccessible or timed out and ordinary direct HTTPS returned 403. ScienceDirect insights pages for the two Elsevier journals returned 403; their readable official shops supplied contribution criteria but undated citation values. Missing current metrics remain empty instead of being filled from third-party aggregators.

Q Bulletin's completed-project/two-cycle rule and WHO/PAHO geographical and public-health relevance are fit conditions. They neither raise prestige automatically nor justify easy-acceptance claims. Regional/institutional journals have no invented acceptance rates.

No venue was contacted, no manuscript submitted, and no fee claim altered. This is independent agent evidence collection and judgment, not human scientific review, an exhaustive search of every editorial report, or manuscript-specific assessment. Recheck official metrics and editorial policies before submission.
